The Catch-Up Act is a smart move to cut through outdated bureaucratic barriers that punish families trying to manage healthcare costs. Current HSA rules—blocking spouses under 55 from contributing—are relics of a system that prioritizes red tape over real solutions. 

The HSA Modernization Act (H.R. 548, Section 8) already lays the groundwork by allowing catch-up contributions for both spouses, proving this isn’t radical—it’s common sense. Medical bankruptcies aren’t caused by families overspending; they’re the result of a rigged system that nickel-and-dimes households while letting hospital monopolies and insurance middlemen jack up prices. Freeing up HSAs lets Americans keep more of their own money to fight back. 

Now let’s go further: audit every line item in the $4.3 trillion healthcare sector to expose where the real waste is.
